newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS end down sharply in Tokyo as energy ebbs.
newsitem.headline: JGBS end down sharply in Tokyo as energy ebbs.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended down sharply but off lows after plunging in morning trade on a strong Bank of Japan (BOJ) tankan report, but afternoon trade was comparatively quiet and 123.00 appeared to be holding as support level, traders said.
But the topside remained heavy on strong Tokyo stocks, and traders added that while it is extremely difficult to predict longer-term direction, sentiment has grown increasingly bearish.
The key September contract ended at 123.05, the lowest since June 11, with turnover of 59,419 contracts.
It had briefly dipped as low as 122.96.

"Since September managed to keep itself above 123.00 at the close, it is unlikely to see sharp falls overnight, as might have happened if it had ended in the 122-123 range," one city bank trader said.

Yield on the benchmark 182nd cash bond was at 2.500 percent, just off a low of 2.505 percent, against 2.340 percent at Tokyo's Tuesday close. The tankan showed that the diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in previous March survey.

Then, a major manufacturers' DI of minus one was forecast for June, a figure that had been factored in by the JGB market, which had been predicting numbers around zero. A Reuters poll of economists produced forecasts for the DI ranging between minus four to plus four.

Traders said that while the market had been shocked by the figures, few felt this would prompt the BOJ to raise interest rates in the immediate future, as the picture for non-manufacturers remains grim. The DI for major non-manufacturers fell to minus seven from minus six and that for small non-manufacturers to minus 11 from minus nine.

Even so, September came under some downward pressure from market talk of an article in the evening edition of a major Japanese daily suggesting that the BOJ won't be able to hold rates at their current ultra-low level. But the article was extremely vague and ultimately had less of an impact on bonds than did a rise in Tokyo stocks, traders said.
The key Nikkei index ended up 337.34 points at 20,679.27 as investor confidence rose on the strong tankan.
The bond market is also very wary about a raft of economic indicators due out Friday, with more sales forecast should they, particularly May industrial production, be strong.
"While 123.00 may hold for now, it's still too early to say the contract's falls are over. A great deal depends on the numbers we see Friday," one trust bank trader said.
May consumer price figures are due out at 0030 GMT Friday, along with jobs data, while the industrial production data is due out at 0430 GMT.

In the JGB market, investment trust firms were detected buying the medium-term zone, while city banks bought the longer end. But activity in afternoon trade was relatively subdued as operators began to turn their eyes to Friday, traders said.
